data.analysis: Keep N=3 and all role identities. T1 currently prescribes two stages without guarding against an oversized or slow final CTA; the source also has an unused warp-reduction helper while reduce0 uses modulo-based interleaving and repeated block synchronization. Refine T1 to test those reduction costs and permit another final stage if measurements warrant it. T2 should not assume a kernel beats the baseline n=1 device copy, which launches no kernel. T3 remains a useful contrast to T1: explicit output initialization plus one atomic per CTA instead of scratch partials. No extra tree is justified.

revisions.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore large-input hierarchical reduction for n=4194304. Replace the current modulo-based interleaved reduction and repeated block-wide synchronization with an efficient warp/block reduction approach, while having CTAs accumulate multiple values per thread from coalesced, disjoint input tiles. Write partials to bounded scratch and reduce them directly to out. Tune tile and block configuration; compare a two-stage path with an additional final reduction stage if the partial count makes a single final CTA inefficient. Cover all legal sizes with bounded reads, exact int32 output, unchanged ABI/default stream, and a correct fallback. Compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline.
